cases.name: Spring Boot migration
cases.objective: Migrate a user-management microservice from Java 8 and Spring Boot 2.7 to Java 21 and Spring Boot 3.2. p0: The Maven build targets Java 21: the `maven.compiler.release` (or equivalent) property in the POM is set to 21, and `mvn clean compile` exits with status code 0 with no compilation errors or warnings related to deprecated or removed Java 8-era APIs.

No source file contains an import of `javax.persistence`, `javax.servlet`, `javax.validation`, or `javax.annotation`; all formerly-Jakarta-EE namespace references use the `jakarta.*` equivalent, and the application context loads without `ClassNotFound` or `NoClassDefFoundError` on startup.

JPA entity mappings and Spring Data JPA repository interfaces compile and run against Hibernate 6 (the version managed by Spring Boot 3.2), with all entity relationships, constraints, and lifecycle callbacks behaving identically to the Java 8 / Hibernate 5 baseline.

Spring Security configuration uses the Spring Security 6 programming model (`SecurityFilterChain` bean with `HttpSecurity` lambda DSL, `AuthenticationManager`/`AuthenticationProvider` wiring as applicable), the JWT filter intercepts and validates tokens, and a request with a valid JWT returns 200 while a request with a missing or expired JWT returns 401.

Role-based access control is enforced: an authenticated user holding a role that is not permitted for a given endpoint receives 403, and an authenticated user holding the required role receives the expected success status, matching the pre-migration authorization matrix.

All REST endpoints that performed create, read, update, and delete on user resources return the same HTTP status codes, response body structure, and side-effects (e.g., 201 with body on create, 200 with body on read, 200 or 204 on update, 204 on delete) as the pre-migration service.

Bean validation (e.g., `@NotNull`, `@Size`, `@Email`, custom validators) on request DTOs produces identical validation error responses (status 400 with the same field-level messages and structure) for invalid input as the pre-migration service.

No source file references `RestTemplate` or `org.springframework.web.client.RestTemplate`; all outbound HTTP calls to external services use `org.springframework.web.client.RestClient`, and the external API integration tests (or contract tests) that verify those outbound interactions pass.

The external API contract is preserved: every endpoint path, HTTP method, accepted request headers, accepted and returned content types, and response JSON/XML schema are unchanged relative to the pre-migration service, as verified by the existing integration or contract test suite.

`mvn clean test` exits with status code 0: all unit tests, integration tests (including those exercising CRUD flows, JWT authentication, role-based authorization, validation error paths, and JPA persistence round-trips), and any external-API interaction tests pass without failures or errors.

`mvn clean compile` exits with status code 0: the full source set compiles under the Java 21 toolchain with Spring Boot 3.2 dependencies, producing class files that the Spring Boot 3.2 application loader can execute.
